correctness.rationale: Verified the exact state-dependent competition k epsilon versus binomial(k,2), hence q_k and the scalar polynomial recurrence. Every skip-1-or-2 path visits at least one member of each pair {2j,2j-1}; its first fresh uniform gives an independent Bernoulli(epsilon/j) variable. First-decision mismatch sums to at most 2epsilon sum_{j>=2}1/j^2; second visited monomers cost at most 4epsilon^2(1-log2); terminal k=2 costs 2epsilon and unpaired odd top costs epsilon/2. Le Cam contributes at most 2epsilon^2 sum 1/j^2, yielding total <5epsilon for epsilon<=1/4. Final compulsory monomer is the deterministic parity map R_n. Harmonic asymptotics, Poisson PGFs and CLT follow. Replayed 294 standalone finite exact/numerical checks; numerical tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The terminal monomer count is a natural finite-size statistic for irreversible competition of single-site and pair deposition. The ratio of successful monomer to dimer rates is approximately 2epsilon/k, so its integrated depletion hazard is epsilon log n and forces a nontrivial 1/log n window. Near terminal depletion matching parity creates an upward-rounded Poisson law, mathematically and physically distinct from conditioning on even/odd Poisson counts. The theorem controls all weak rates with an explicit uniform total-variation estimate, includes two different parity limiting PGFs and a large-mean Gaussian crossover, and resolves the natural distinction between competition-induced versus compulsory monomers; not simply parity arithmetic or a known Gibbs-table recomputation.
